Personally, I like my speedball oblique with a pointed nib, and FW blue pearlescent ink.

What pen (brand or type!), script, and/or ink do you prefer?

I used to use a custom turned oblique pen from a local craftsman, though I seem to have misplaced it during my long hiatus from calligraphy. All I can find now is my Century olbique from paperinkarts. My scripts of choice are Engrosser's and Textura Quadrata, though it's been a long time since they've been practiced. I use walnut / hydrated peat moss as ink, for cost-effective practicing, and Higgins eternal or Windsor & Newton for finished pieces.
I'm curious where you find walnut/hydrated peat moss for purchase. It sounds like something you concoct at home yourself. How does it work?

I get both of them from this page here. The "Walnut Ink Crystals" are supposedly dehydrated peat moss of a sort, or so I've heard.

To be entirely honest, I have no idea how the crystals work. You can make walnut ink at home, there's a few good recipes, this one comes to mind. I would have done it by now but for a woeful lack of walnuts where I am.

I use Pilot Parallel Pens and inks. There are some crazy things you can do with them, and they are really solid, flow nicely, and I just like them. I have a set of dip-pens and one set of more 'traditional' pens with proper nibs but use an ink cartridge. I prefer the parallel pens though.

I have the largest parallel pen, and I really loved it when I bought it. But it guzzles ink like crazy, and I don't really use it anymore. It definitely has its place, but I just don't care for it anymore.

I have a few Pilot Parallel Pens still in their original packaging that I received for my birthday from a family member who knew I was interested in learning calligraphy. I'm hoping they will be useful for picking up the basics!
They are! I used some makers to start but the parallel pens really help to teach you about pressure and position when writing.

For everyday practice, I stick with my trusty Manuscript pen and ink. It may not be a unique-high-quality-super-expensive pen like some of the other ones I've seen, but I'll be damned if it doesn't do a great job. I've had the same pen for almost two years now and it still works perfectly.

I've been meaning to get some Brause nibs though. I've heard great things about them. Also, I bought a bottle of Iroshizuku Murasaki-Shikibu ink and it is absolutely beautiful. Well worth the $17 on Amazon.

I know it's not trees related, and I don't particularly condone hard drug use, but we have a growing and accepting community at /v/opiates if that's your thing, or you're just curious. Again, don't take this as an invitation to start using heroin, but if you're already a user, it's a safe place for discussion and help. Once we grow a little bit, we'll be starting a recovery subverse, as well.

No problem, I just wanted to create a safe place for active opiate users, recovering addicts, and even just people who are curious about us and our lifestyle to congregate and discuss things.

Our forum is for discussions such as: the issues opiate users uniquely face, what's called "stamp reports" (heroin on the east side of the country comes in little paper envelopes, and different batches have different ink stamps on them, so stamp reports are just reports on whether different stamps have good, bad, dangerous, strong, weak, or bunk heroin in them, sort of like pill reports for ecstasy pills), dope porn (exactly what it sounds like: pics of drugs, basically, sometimes with naked people in them), news on opiate laws and the current opiate epidemic in the United States, advice with anything a user might experience medically (even if it's something common and well-understood, like dosages, histamine reactions, or lumps caused by missing the vein, people can be very comforted just by hearing that they're not gonna die or anything), legal advice from people who have already lived it, sharing creative writing stories (this is my favorite; an opiate user's experiences make for some absolutely incredible stories), and all of this and more with a focus on harm reduction.

People are gonna do what they're gonna do, even if we tell them they shouldn't, and it's a much better technique to try and help them do it safely, rather than parrot "don't do drugs!" while they do it anyways, just with no advice and with them winging it. Doesn't stop me from trying, though; if someone comes in and is like "I tried vicodin and loved how it made me feel, and I found a guy who will sell me Percocet; how much should I take to feel good?" I always preface my answer with some variant of "walk away, doing this will start you down an irreversible path leading to serious addiction and harder opiates, and no matter how much you feel in control now, that WILL change, it does for absolutely everyone." They never listen, but I HAVE to try, even if I give them the advice they're looking for immediately after so they don't OD.

Anyways, I didn't mean to rant, but I feel pretty passionately about this subject and this subverse I'm working on, and now you have an idea of what it's about. I hope anyone reading this who uses or will use opiates joins us, for their own safety's sake.
